Title: Export file name carries a random 6-digit token on the shipped default template
Preconditions: A primary currency is configured (some currency has isPrimary=true) — without one the export job aborts before a file name is built. CatalogCsvImport.ExportFileNameTemplate has NO saved value (itHasValues=false).
Test_Data: {{BACK_URL}}; {{ADMIN_EMAIL}}; {{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}; catalogId resolved by live-discover (never hardcode a catalog GUID)
Steps:
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token — grant_type=password, username={{ADMIN_EMAIL}}, password={{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}
[API] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings/CatalogCsvImport.ExportFileNameTemplate — confirm itHasValues=false and that defaultValue ends with the random parameter
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/catalog/catalogs/search {"take":50} — live-discover the first non-virtual catalog; capture catalogId
[API] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/catalogcsvimport/export/mappingconfiguration?catalogId=<catalogId> — capture the response as configuration
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/catalogcsvimport/export with {catalogId, configuration, currency} — capture the notification id
[API] poll POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/pushnotifications {"take":20} until the CatalogCsvExport notification with that id has finished set; capture downloadUrl
Assertions:
[FORMAT] the downloadUrl file name matches ^products_\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}_\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{2}_\d{6}\.csv$ {OBSERVED}
[API] the notification reports errorCount=0 and processedCount equal to totalCount {OBSERVED}
Cross_Layer_Checks: [NETWORK] GET the downloadUrl — HTTP 200 and a non-empty CSV whose first line is the column header, proving the rename did not break export content {OBSERVED}
Failure_Signals:
A name with no trailing 6-digit segment means the fix is not deployed — check the module version is at least 3.1004.0.
An errors[] entry "Primary currency not found" is an environment misconfiguration, not a product defect.
Cleanup: Exported CSV stays in the temp blob container; no teardown required.

Title: Two consecutive exports never produce the same file name
Preconditions: A primary currency is configured (some currency has isPrimary=true) — without one the export job aborts before a file name is built. CatalogCsvImport.ExportFileNameTemplate has NO saved value (itHasValues=false).
Test_Data: {{BACK_URL}}; {{ADMIN_EMAIL}}; {{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}; catalogId resolved by live-discover (never hardcode a catalog GUID)
Steps:
[API] reuse the auth, catalog-discovery, mapping-configuration, export and polling sequence unchanged (state from CSVIO-019); capture downloadUrl — first run
[API] reuse the auth, catalog-discovery, mapping-configuration, export and polling sequence unchanged (state from CSVIO-019); capture downloadUrl — second run, started immediately after the first finishes
Assertions:
[FORMAT] both file names match the products_<date>_<time>_<6 digits>.csv shape {OBSERVED}
[STATE] the two file names differ — the random segment is redrawn per export, so even a same-second repeat cannot collide {OBSERVED}
Cross_Layer_Checks: [NETWORK] both downloadUrl values return HTTP 200 — the second export must not overwrite the first blob {OBSERVED}
Failure_Signals:
Identical names mean the random segment is not redrawn per export (cached or per-process), which reinstates the guessable-URL defect.
Only one of the two blobs being retrievable means the names collided and the second export overwrote the first.
Cleanup: Exported CSV stays in the temp blob container; no teardown required.

Title: Template without the random parameter still produces the pre-upgrade file name shape
Preconditions: A primary currency is configured (isPrimary=true). The account may write platform settings. CSVIO-019 has run once so its export sequence is established.
Test_Data: {{BACK_URL}}; {{ADMIN_EMAIL}}; {{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}; catalogId resolved by live-discover (never hardcode a catalog GUID)
Steps:
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings — set CatalogCsvImport.ExportFileNameTemplate to products_{0:yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss}
[API] reuse the auth, catalog-discovery, mapping-configuration, export and polling sequence unchanged (state from CSVIO-019); capture downloadUrl
Assertions:
[FORMAT] the file name matches ^products_\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}_\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{2}\.csv$ with no trailing 6-digit segment {OBSERVED}
[API] the export finishes with errorCount=0 — an unused format argument must not throw {OBSERVED}
Failure_Signals:
A random segment appearing anyway means the saved template is ignored in favour of the default, which breaks every integration parsing the old name shape.
An export failure here means an unused format argument now throws, which would be a backward-compatibility regression.
Cleanup: Restore CatalogCsvImport.ExportFileNameTemplate to unset by saving a whitespace-only value — the platform normalises it to null and itHasValues returns to false.

Title: Invalid template with an out-of-range parameter index fails the export loudly instead of producing a file (negative)
Preconditions: A primary currency is configured (isPrimary=true). The account may write platform settings. CSVIO-019 has run once so its export sequence is established. The [ADMIN] assertion needs a catalog that HAS items — the Export toolbar command renders disabled on an empty catalog, so a live-discovered empty catalog makes that step unreachable (STOP, not a failure).
Test_Data: {{BACK_URL}}; {{ADMIN_EMAIL}}; {{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}; catalogId resolved by live-discover (never hardcode a catalog GUID)
Steps:
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings — set CatalogCsvImport.ExportFileNameTemplate to products_{0:yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss}_{2}, an index the code does not supply
[API] reuse the auth, catalog-discovery, mapping-configuration, export and polling sequence unchanged (state from CSVIO-019); capture downloadUrl
Cross_Layer_Checks: [ADMIN] the export blade surfaces the failure — the error count and error list render, rather than the blade staying on its starting state {SPEC}
Failure_Signals:
The export reporting success, or producing a downloadable file, means the invalid index was silently swallowed and the file name is not what the template says.
A file appearing in the temp container despite the reported failure means a partially built name was used and the export wrote to an unintended path.
The notification never reaching a finished state means the job died before updating it, a different defect from a formatting failure.
The blade staying on its starting state means an admin typo disables catalog export with no visible signal.
Cleanup: Restore CatalogCsvImport.ExportFileNameTemplate to unset by saving a whitespace-only value — the platform normalises it to null and itHasValues returns to false.
References: VCST-5745; Observed: 2026-08-27 on vcst, CatalogCsvImportModule 3.1004.0 — this wording re-verified green in REG-2026-08-27-1410 (tmp container 225 blobs before and after; notification errorCount=1, processed/total=0, downloadUrl=null; blade rendered Export failed + the error list) — the export fails, the blade renders Export failed / Error count 1 / the error list, and no blob is written. BY DESIGN, deliberately not asserted here: there is no save-time validation of the template, because the setting description itself documents the supported parameters ({0} timestamp, {1} random 6-digit) — see CSVIO-026 — so an out-of-range index is out-of-contract input rather than a missing guard. The runtime diagnostic is the raw framework FormatException text; recorded as observed, not asserted. Supersedes the 2026-08-18 note claiming no admin-visible error — that is no longer true.

Title: Export file name template setting documents both parameters in the localized admin UI
Preconditions: Admin SPA reachable; at least two UI languages available.
Steps:
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token — grant_type=password, username={{ADMIN_EMAIL}}, password={{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}
[API] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/localization?lang=en — read catalogCsvImportModule.settings.ExportFileNameTemplate
[API] repeat for at least one non-English language, for example ru and de
[NAV] {{ADMIN_URL}} — Settings, search CSV, open the General group
[ACT] locate the field labelled "Export file name template"
[ACT] read the description text rendered under that field
Assertions:
[DOM] the description text under the "Export file name template" field contains the literal substrings "{0}" and "{1}", the worked example "products_{0:yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss}_{1}", and a sentence stating the .csv extension is added automatically {OBSERVED}
[FORMAT] the "{0}" and "{1}" placeholders appear verbatim in every language checked — neither interpolated into a value nor stripped from the text {OBSERVED}
Cross_Layer_Checks: [ADMIN] the template value prefilled in the field matches the defaultValue the settings API reports for CatalogCsvImport.ExportFileNameTemplate {OBSERVED}
Failure_Signals:
A localization mentioning only the timestamp parameter means a translator dropped the new one, so admins in that language cannot discover the feature.
A description showing an interpolated date instead of the literal placeholder means the translation pipeline treats it as a format argument.
References: VCST-5745; Observed: 2026-08-18 — en, ru and de all carry both parameters

Title: A format specifier on the random parameter still renders exactly six digits
Preconditions: A primary currency is configured (isPrimary=true). The account may write platform settings. CSVIO-019 has run once so its export sequence is established.
Test_Data: {{BACK_URL}}; {{ADMIN_EMAIL}}; {{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}; catalogId resolved by live-discover (never hardcode a catalog GUID)
Steps:
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings — set CatalogCsvImport.ExportFileNameTemplate to products_{1:D6}, the specifier an admin would reasonably add to force six digits
[API] reuse the auth, catalog-discovery, mapping-configuration, export and polling sequence unchanged (state from CSVIO-019); capture downloadUrl
Assertions:
[FORMAT] the file name matches ^products_\d{6}\.csv$ — the specifier is ignored rather than fatal, because the token is passed to string.Format pre-formatted as a string {SPEC}
[API] the notification reports errorCount=0, so a specifier on a non-IFormattable argument did not throw {SPEC}
Cross_Layer_Checks: [NETWORK] GET the downloadUrl returns HTTP 200 and a non-empty CSV {SPEC}
Failure_Signals:
A FormatException means the token stopped being passed as a padded string — the design note in the ticket calls this out as the reason for the string, so a regression here reintroduces the 1-to-6-digit variability the padding removes.
A name carrying the literal D6 means the parameter was rendered without being formatted at all.
Cleanup: Restore CatalogCsvImport.ExportFileNameTemplate to unset by saving a whitespace-only value — the platform normalises it to null and itHasValues returns to false.
References: VCST-5745; spec source: ExportFileNameHelperTests.GetFileName_RandomNumberWithFormatSpecifier_StillRendersSixDigits (deleted in PR #145 commit 5581fd1)
